title: Bite-vector comment says the broken branch makes the route FLIP to m2; the actual (toggle-verified) behavior is count 0 — the route VANISHES
evidence: core/routing_cost_test.odin:225-226: `//       re-priced) bundle cost the edge would price at narrow's 20 and` / `//       the route would FLIP to m2 (20+5=25 > 20) — the bite vector;`; core/routing.odin:178-179: `nd := dist[cur] + cat.pipe_tiers[t.pipe_tier[pi]].cost` / `if dist[ns] == UNREACHABLE || nd < dist[ns] {`; core/routing.odin:221-222: `} else if c < min_cost[ns] {` / `min_cost[ns] = c // a fatter (cheaper) member re-prices the edge`; core/routing.odin:238: `if dist[ns] + min_cost[ns] != dist[u] {`
detail: Removing the branch keeps min_cost=20 while dist(res)=10 via per-pipe relaxation; pass 2 rejects m1 (25!=10) and m2 (20!=10): count 0, route VANISHES — matching the PR body's documented toggle result. 'FLIP to m2' contradicts the code; toggle-verified.
recommended_fix: Reword the comment: with re-pricing broken the edge stays 20, no neighbor satisfies dist(v)+min_cost==dist(u), so (res,host) gets count 0 — the route vanishes; the count-1 assert fails.

title: hops[int(off)] and bundle_slot/rep_slot derefs run after non-fatal expectf checks — in the bite scenario they mis-read the adjacent hop row instead of the pinned message
evidence: core/routing_cost_test.odin:254-258: `testing.expectf(t, count == 1,` / `"the re-priced fat bundle must win UNIQUELY (count 1), got %d", count)` / `testing.expectf(t, s.routing.hops[int(off)].node == m1,` / `"next hop must be m1 (bundle priced at its min member: 5+5=10), got %d — the bundle edge was NOT re-priced",` / `s.routing.hops[int(off)].node)`; core/routing_cost_test.odin:282-288: `testing.expectf(t, rep_slot != -1, "the res-m1 bundle must have a live member")` / `testing.expectf(t, s.topology.pipe_tier[rep_slot] == narrow,` / `testing.expectf(t, s.routing.hops[int(off)].pipe == s.topology.pipe_id[rep_slot],`; core/routing_cost_test.odin:292-293: `testing.expectf(t, s.bundles.bundle_count[bundle_slot] == 2,` / `"mixed-tier bundle holds 2 members, got %d", s.bundles.bundle_count[bundle_slot])`
detail: expectf records and CONTINUES; in the documented bite scenario count==0 and hops[int(off)] mis-reads the adjacent (m1,host) row — my toggle run printed 'got 3' and 'got 2' — misleading failures, not the pinned message. r1 note #3's guard fix unapplied to the new pin.
recommended_fix: Guard the derefs: `if count == 1` before the hops[int(off)] reads; `if rep_slot != -1` before pipe_tier[rep_slot]; `if bfound` before the bundle_count/cap/tier reads.

title: The reverse-direction expectf passes even with the re-pricing branch removed — no W1 bite in reverse, and its '(re-priced bundle, 5+5=10)' attribution is misleading
evidence: core/routing_cost_test.odin:260-262: `nh, _, oknh := routing_next_hop(&s.routing, &s.topology, host, res)` / `testing.expectf(t, oknh && nh == m1,` / `"host's next hop toward res must be m1 (re-priced bundle, 5+5=10), got ok=%v nh=%d", oknh, nh)`
detail: Toggle-verified: with the branch removed only lines 254/256/286 fail — the reverse expectf still passes (host->m1 is one wide pipe, min==representative cost; dist[m1]=5 comes from the wide member's per-pipe relaxation). No re-pricing involved; the comment overstates the check's coverage.
recommended_fix: Reword the reverse comment (the result holds with the branch broken); optionally make the reverse check re-price-dependent, or drop it since the forward count-1 assert already bites.
